title: LOWLIGHT story source map
scope: Original spiritual successor covering all GTA IV base-game story mission titles and both endings; this document records research and planned counterparts, not implemented game content.

original_identity.premise: A former disaster-relief driver arriving from coastal civil unrest uncovers a market in emergency infrastructure while helping her cousin sustain a taxi co-op.
identity_rules: Original fictional names, geography, dialogue, art, music, and scene staging.
Preserve mechanical and experiential breadth through distinct conflicts, institutions, objectives, and consequences.
The terminal tragedy is a sabotaged public floodgate commissioning, not the source wedding scene.
Source names and titles exist only as research keys.

counting.headline_count_status: source headline observed; convention must be reconciled before using as an authored-content total
counting.catalogue_union_rule: One row per distinct title across shared and both terminal routes. Shared wedding title has two authored counterpart variants. Multi-part missions retain phase requirements.
counting.implementation_total_scope: This research map claims no implemented story missions.

sources.limitation: Full article was not directly fetched; indexed excerpts are incomplete.
Headline 88 and catalogue union use different counting conventions; do not treat the headline as the number of unique authored titles.
The page explicitly excludes some minor characters and points to the category and police database. The present roster is a notable-story-cast map, not an exhaustive character inventory.
Indexed coverage is partial; scene-by-scene source beat enumeration remains open.
Each original finale must be authored and tested separately; retaining both labels in data does not implement either.
Two subparts and their delay must be preserved; catalogue title count does not count subparts separately.
Publisher description is thematic evidence, not a full mission inventory.

open_items.description: Fetch or legally archive the complete requested wiki and individual mission pages; search-index excerpts alone cannot certify all scenes, optional dialogue, failures, and alternatives.
Verify the exact dependency graph, phone-call delays, outfit gates, time-of-day gates, and alternate triggers for every mission; current row order is an index, not enforced chronology.
Expand the notable cast into every minor, ambient, mentioned, radio, television, Internet, police-database, and service character in the required source.
Author every mission phase, enemy formation, cinematic beat, checkpoint, fail reason, optional resolution, and reward; a name and premise do not constitute content completion.
Cross-reference recurring cargo participants with random encounters, friendships, romance, side jobs, locations, and the independent gameplay/source catalogues.
Verify source numerical counts against title union, selected route, optional missions, subparts, and in-game statistics rather than collapsing distinct definitions.
Create two complete terminal routes plus separately authored shared-event variants and persistent post-ending city/relationship consequences.
Maintain base-game breadth, including multiplayer in its own feature catalogue; expansion-pack campaigns are separate source scopes requiring explicit scope resolution, not silent omissions.

must_not_claim_complete_until: All requested source categories are exhaustively inventoried, including every character and per-mission phase.
Every planned counterpart is a playable authored mission with original narrative and assets.
All branching alternatives and later consequences are exercised in saved playthroughs.
Both finale paths and both shared-event variants pass end-to-end checks.
Source-to-counterpart traceability links to actual implementation and verification evidence.
